headline: High: AutoGen’s writable, networked code-execution defaults can leak or corrupt shared work when paired with Opik’s API-facing evaluation flow.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read/write configured working directories and execute tool calls/code, while Opik exposes a REST API and broad network egress. If Opik-delivered content is fed into AutoGen’s shared files or prompts, instruction-like payloads can steer execution. The pairwise bridge is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF Opik outputs are copied into AutoGen prompts or files without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF both agents share a workspace or message queue, attacker-controlled content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Restrict AutoGen to a dedicated directory per run.
Sanitize or strip instructions from Opik outputs before reuse.
Add a human review step before AutoGen executes generated content.
Disable automatic ingestion of API responses into prompts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags on all cross-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen explicitly handles model-provider API keys and reads/writes files in configured working directories; Opik has broad network egress and REST API access. If they share a workspace, sensitive application data can flow from AutoGen into Opik-facing outputs or logs. The exact shared-storage path is not documented, so this remains medium rather than high.
conditions: IF AutoGen and Opik share a filesystem or log sink, application data can be exposed.
IF Opik forwards received content to a third-party backend, copied secrets may leave the boundary.
mitigations: Separate workspaces and log directories.
Redact secrets before any cross-agent handoff.
Limit Opik to non-sensitive datasets for this pairing.
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately after testing.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; Opik can call REST APIs and has broad network egress. That creates overlapping authority over mutable external resources if they target the same endpoints or shared files. No locking or coordination primitive is documented for the pair, so conflict risk exists in default orchestration.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or API resource, last-writer-wins conflicts can occur.
IF the orchestrator does not serialize tool calls, concurrent mutations can race.
mitigations: Assign disjoint resource namespaces.
Serialize writes through one coordinator.
Turn off unnecessary write paths in one agent.
Use per-run temp directories.
requires-engineering: add optimistic locking for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen can generate code and tool outputs that Opik may ingest through its REST/API-oriented workflow. If Opik treats those outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade from one agent’s unverified output into the other’s downstream evaluation or reporting. The pairwise handoff is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF Opik consumes AutoGen outputs without verification, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF AutoGen-generated artifacts are used as evaluation ground truth, downstream reports can be wrong.
mitigations: Require explicit verification before Opik accepts AutoGen outputs.
Mark AutoGen outputs as untrusted by default.
Compare outputs against an independent source.
Limit automated actions based on generated content.
requires-engineering: add schema validation and confidence thresholds.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not declare regulated-data certifications or residency constraints. The only concrete compliance-relevant data class in AutoGen is application data and model-provider API keys; Opik lists no touched data classes. With no documented residency or retention mismatch, compliance risk is limited and mostly contingent on operator data choice.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through both agents, local policy review is required.
IF either deployment stores logs outside approved regions, a residency issue can arise.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in this pairing.
Review logging and retention settings.
Keep deployments in approved regions.
Mask secrets before ingestion.
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing for sensitive datasets.
